Prevention: Mow or shred ground fruit to kill the larvae or expose them to other predators
Remove unwanted and unmanaged fruit trees to reduce the source of breeding sites for fruit fly
Pick up and dispose of fallen fruits by deep burying (cover the fruits in a pit with at least 30 cm of soil)
Remove late hanging fruits missed during harvest
Create awareness about the problem by informing other growers
Monitoring: Use traps and lures to detect presence and severity of fruit fly infestation
Inspect trees for presences of fruit fly
Collect any missed and fallen fruit and inspect them for presence of larvae

Look for small (pin head size) brown/black patches on the fruit - appear around the place of oviposition and the infested fruits start rotting check out for “crying” fruits (fluids oozing out of wounds) on the tree
Direct Control: Traps are not a management strategy for fruit flies but give an indication of infestation.
Instead use baits or lure if fruits flies have been observed
Bait mixture is prepared using an attractant (molasses, alcohol and jackfruit) source) and an insecticide (Malathion) are effective.
Encourage fellow mango farmers to use the baited lures to avoid their orchards acting as breeding grounds for fruit fly
To check the carry-over of the pest, collect and destroy all fallen and attacked fruits.
Restrictions: input daelers and always read the label for direction on pesticide use use
Always wear protective gear (overalls, gumboots, goggles, caps, gloves and face masks) when handling chemicals
Organically acceptable fruit fly bait containing a food attractant and the insecticide
